source.compiler: the Hockey Databank, version 13.0 of 10 July 2018 (maintained through the hockey-databank Yahoo group), as published at github.com/rippinrobr/hockey-databank
source.conversion: computed from each player's regular seasons 1962/63, 1961/62, 1960/61 (weighted 3:2:1; docs/design/computed-ratings.md, steps 3 to 5): a player's value is selection and production as z-scores over the season's regulars (a quarter of the window's games), weighted selection:production forwards 0.15:0.85 (prior 9.8, replacement 0.329, 72 regulars of 86), defencemen 0.25:0.75 (prior 20, replacement 0.3, 35 regulars of 50), goalies 0.6:0.4 (prior 14.8, replacement 0.0507, 8 regulars of 15), tuned once on EA's NHLPA 93, NHL 94, NHL 95, NHL 07 and NHL 22. Selection is his share of the club's games (a goalie's: of its minutes) over the seasons of the window he played. Production is points a game for skaters and, for goalies, goals against under the league's an hour (no shots against were kept for the whole window), pooled over the window and shrunk toward replacement (the pooled rate of the quarter of the group with the least exposure) by the prior, the noise per unit of exposure over the regulars' talent variance, on each record's effective exposure (Σw·e)²/Σw²·e. A player plays for the club he played most games for (a tie: the later one). Each club's squad is picked by provisional ratings (each value's mid-rank in its group over the season's 151 players); then every squad player's rating is his value's mid-rank in his group over the season's 135 squad players, read off NHL 27's squads in that group (scripts/data/nhl-seasons.json computed.histograms: forwards 433, defenders 236, goalies 64); ties stay ties and nobody passes anybody in a group. A player outside the squads takes the rating of the highest squad value in his group not above his. Then every club is moved toward its real results: S is each club's goal differential a game from the Hockey Databank's Teams.csv (a shoot-out's goal taken off both sides; × (n − 1) ÷ n, a club meeting the other n − 1), its reliability from Poisson goals, reliability r 0.775; m, the match model's margin a game per point of a lineup's played strength (the mean of its attack and defence) under the season's rules, is 0.3078 goals (at scoring 1.04); each club's target is the clubs' mean before the move + √r × S ÷ m, and every player of the club moves by one whole number, its best few one point more, whichever brings its lineup nearest the target (no player passes one rated above him in his club). Every player's lines and the season's results are in scripts/data/nhl-seasons/nhl-1963.json.
